scope: Independent read-only source review and one final run of the two targeted Node test files. Native browser evidence was executed by tooltip_ux and independently inspected here; it is not a second browser run. No production edits by this cross-review.

independentTests.method: Deterministic JavaScript tests, using small DOM/event doubles where applicable. No browser/layout/physical-touch claim.

nativeEvidenceInspected.nativeAdjacentAndBulkClicks: Passed without Escape, force, or dispatch in all five desktop widths; ephemeral selection and complete persisted state checked separately.
nativeEvidenceInspected.passiveSelectionQualification: Native text selection moved focus from BUTTON i99 to BODY. Space/Enter/Ctrl+A preserved materials/save in that observed state. The separate case where a card remains focused is protected in source and covered by deterministic tests, not claimed as the native focus state.
nativeEvidenceInspected.touchScope: 390x844 emulated touch, including compatibility mouseover after closing the dialog. No physical touch device claim.

reviewed: Placement excludes the full item pool, settlement, dock, own anchor, details trigger, and all currently measured visible-sized interactive controls. Rectangle splitting deduplicates and removes contained regions at each step; no fit returns the explicit-dialog path.
The passive panel remains pointer-interactive and internally scrollable. Its safe area can be short; the visible details button and F2 expose the complete dialog.

Four-direction anchor-to-panel corridors retain the item while a real pointer journey crosses intermediate cards; exiting the corridor resumes ordinary hover. The journey latch starts only on departure from the active anchor, so a focus-only preview does not capture unrelated later hover.
Escape cancels pending timers, suppresses redisplay during same-anchor internal movement and removes stale aria-describedby. True exit/re-entry and fresh keyboard focus can restore access.
Passive text reading blocks material shortcuts; Enter and Space prevent default activation when the event target remains an item anchor. Ctrl+A retains native selection behavior.
The modal focuses its scrollable content, retains native text selection and scrolling, cycles its close/content focus with Tab, and restores eligible item focus on close.

Notice-only and undo-expiry refreshes retain an open dialog; a different game-state object, target set, or committed action closes stale detail content. Body-level dialog content is excluded from app-scoped focus restoration.
Touch pointer events suppress compatibility hover briefly after dismissal; keyboard input restores intentional hover/focus behavior.

Inspection changes ephemeral UI state only; inventory mutations continue through the existing act/save transaction path. No engine, RNG, save schema or equipment-catalog changes are introduced by the tooltip patch.
Fusion comparison labels agree with the shared affix descriptions: shield bypass, resonance-critical follow chance, survival recovery, main-hit fraction for follow damage, and chest-only gold.

findings.issue: Earlier native candidates could switch inspected equipment while crossing intermediate cards and cover visible action controls. Final corridor/control exclusion source, targeted tests and owner native assertions address both. Earlier failures are retained by the owner; this report does not relabel their candidates as passed.

A native assertion label mentions a focused card during text reading, but recorded focus after selection is BODY. This report limits its native conclusion to the actual recorded focus; focused-anchor default prevention is supported by source and deterministic tests.
No additional defect found in the scoped final source and tests. This does not certify unmeasured layouts or input devices.

historicalReview.counting: Preserved unchanged; not final-source proof and not added to the final 14-test count.
historicalReview.rejectedBaselineHypothesis: The owner observed baseline Escape at 7.8 ms before the 160 ms pending-show timer and no reopening after 350 ms. A baseline timer-escape defect is not asserted.

limitations: The independent Node tests use deterministic DOM/event doubles and cannot establish pixel geometry, accessibility certification, real keyboard dispatch or physical touch behavior.
Real Chromium layout/input evidence is the separately attributed owner report, with synthetic saves. Native screenshot aesthetics were not independently re-rendered in this review.
The final browser assertions cover five desktop widths and one narrow emulated-touch viewport, not every viewport, display scale or assistive technology.
No screen-reader, physical mobile device, Windows double-click startup, hardware GPU or long-term human play validation is claimed here.
The separate 30-window performance diagnosis did not enter fusion and is not evidence of fusion throughput or frame-rate improvement.
